items.text: L – Left-to-right ventricular or atrial septal shunting.

blocks.text: Add PDA, which is also a left-to-right shunt after birth.
Acyanotic defects generally do not produce central cyanosis initially because oxygenated blood enters the pulmonary circulation rather than bypassing it.
Large unrepaired left-to-right shunts may eventually cause pulmonary hypertension and Eisenmenger syndrome, resulting in cyanosis.

content_groups.group_title: Tetralogy of Fallot: the four components

blocks.text: Children with Tetralogy of Fallot may develop hypercyanotic spells (Tet spells), often precipitated by crying, feeding or exertion.
Squatting or the knee-chest position increases systemic vascular resistance and can reduce right-to-left shunting.

blocks.text: Remember: Cyanosis is not always a reliable indicator of hypoxaemia. Its visibility depends on the absolute concentration of deoxygenated haemoglobin, perfusion and other factors.
Mnemonic: SEVEN – Features favouring an innocent murmur.

items.text: V – Variable with posture or respiration.
N – No associated abnormal cardiac signs or symptoms.
L – Loud murmur, particularly grade 3/6 or above.
U – Unusual timing: diastolic or continuous (unless a recognised innocent continuous murmur).
D – Diffuse radiation or abnormal associated symptoms.

blocks.text: Important clinical note: A murmur's intensity alone does not reliably determine the severity of the underlying lesion. A small VSD may produce a loud murmur, while a large VSD may produce a softer murmur.

blocks.text: Rheumatic heart disease follows acute rheumatic fever, which develops after infection with group A beta-haemolytic Streptococcus (Streptococcus pyogenes), usually pharyngitis.
The disease results from an autoimmune reaction due to molecular mimicry between streptococcal antigens and host tissues.

items.text: T – Tissue damage and chronic scarring.
M – Mitral valve: most commonly affected.
A – Aortic valve: second most commonly affected.
V – Valvular disease, including stenosis and regurgitation.

blocks.text: Rheumatic heart disease is not caused by the bacteria directly invading the heart. It is an immune-mediated consequence of a preceding group A streptococcal infection.

blocks.text: OSCE pearl: Myocarditis should be suspected in a child with recent viral illness followed by unexplained tachycardia, respiratory distress, hepatomegaly, chest pain or signs of heart failure.
